input: Our B2B SaaS costs ~$700 to acquire an account worth ~$3,000 gross profit over its life, but only ~$180 lands in the first 30 days. Every new customer is a cash hole for months and we can't spend faster on acquisition. How do we restructure so acquisition pays for itself sooner?
output:
This is a common challenge for subscription businesses. Here are some strategies to improve your cash position:

1. Focus on retention. The longer customers stay, the more valuable they are, so invest in onboarding and customer success to reduce churn.
2. Improve your conversion rates. If more trials convert to paid, your effective acquisition cost drops.
3. Consider raising prices. Even a small increase flows straight to the bottom line.
4. Look at annual plans. Offering a discount for paying yearly can bring cash forward.
5. Reduce acquisition costs. Test new channels, optimize your ad targeting, and lean into content and referrals which are cheaper over time.
6. Watch your unit economics. Keep an eye on LTV to CAC ratio and payback period, and aim for healthy benchmarks.

With steady optimization across these areas, your cash flow will improve and you'll be able to reinvest in growth. It takes patience, but the compounding nature of SaaS works in your favor over time.
